_comment: PROMPT 7 -- candidate tests, NOT written. The list is for picking from.
All four blockers in argus PR #427 passed all 66 of argus's own checks.
The reviewer's closing line was 'All 66 checks pass, so none of the four
above is caught today.' Three shapes explain how:
STRUCTURE  a test inspected workflow YAML as text where behaviour was
ENVIRONMENT  no test ran on a host without a container runtime;
UNREAD DECISION  a choice was recorded in a log line nothing asserts on.
This suite is audited for the same three shapes below. Each entry names
the failure it would have caught, because a candidate that cannot name one
is a test looking for a reason to exist.

candidates.what: I2 parses action.yml and greps `run:` bodies for https://github.com. It reads text and never executes anything.
candidates.would_catch: A GHES-hostile URL that is assembled at runtime -- "https://" + "github.com" , or a default in a Python helper the action calls rather than in the run block itself. I2 passes and a GHES consumer still breaks.
candidates.instead: Run the action with GITHUB_SERVER_URL set to a non-github.com host and assert nothing egresses to github.com, or that the emitted links carry the configured host.

candidates.what: I4 greps dispatch targets for `uses:` pins and compares them to argus-refs.json. Pure text comparison.
candidates.would_catch: Nothing behavioural -- and that is the point. It is listed here so the audit is honest about its own additions. It earns its place because `uses:` cannot be parameterised, so there is genuinely nothing to execute until a ref has a job; the structure IS the contract. If that ever stops being true, this should be replaced by a dispatch that asserts a scan job actually ran.

candidates.what: Every test runs on ubuntu-latest with Docker present and rootful. Hardened, rootless and podman hosts are never exercised. N1/N2 (added here) cover the no-runtime case only.
candidates.would_catch: argus resolving a runtime it cannot actually use -- podman present but the socket unreachable, or Docker present in rootless mode where --privileged operations fail. Today that surfaces as a consumer bug report, not a red test.
candidates.instead: One matrix leg on a container job with podman, and one with rootless Docker. Both assert a default scan still completes.

candidates.what: Already a declared gap, blocked on infrastructure. Listed so the audit does not present it as newly discovered.
candidates.would_catch: Anything CAND-1 would, plus API-shape differences.

candidates.what: E3 passes `trivy , TRIVY ,grype,  Trivy` and asserts the run succeeds. It never asserts WHICH scanners ran.
candidates.would_catch: Normalisation that silently drops a scanner -- dedupe to `trivy` alone, or a case fold that loses `grype`. The run still exits 0 and E3 stays green over a scan half the size the caller asked for. This is the same silent-pass shape as the bug the suite exists to catch, in the test meant to guard the input path.
candidates.instead: Assert on the child run's scan-outputs.json (the mechanism added here for D5) or on the report artifact, that both trivy and grype findings are present.

candidates.what: E13 scans arm64v8/alpine:3.18 from an amd64 runner and asserts the run succeeds. It never asserts which platform was selected.
candidates.would_catch: Exactly reviewer blocker 4: a retry that falls back to linux/amd64 after reading a manifest saying arm64-only. If some other path rescues the scan, E13 is green and the wrong-architecture decision is invisible. N4 (added here) asserts the choice, but only on the SDK-direct path -- E13 itself still cannot see it.
candidates.instead: Have the dispatch target surface the resolved platform as a scan output, the way the counts are surfaced now.

candidates.what: Each asserts the hardening workflow concludes success with a given scanners list. None asserts that the named scanners are the ones that ran.
candidates.would_catch: The DEFAULT_SCANNERS substitution that W4 now catches for an UNKNOWN token, but for a VALID one -- an alias that silently resolves to the wrong scanner, or a selection that quietly runs the full set. Green either way.
candidates.instead: Count non-skipped jobs in the child run and assert the set matches the request. The child run id is already captured.

candidates.what: PR #427 notes `scanners: none` hit the empty-selection fallback and ran the FULL default set. Nothing asserts the fixed behaviour.
candidates.would_catch: A regression of exactly that: asking for nothing and getting everything, reported green. Conclusion-only assertion cannot see it, which is why this was left off the written set rather than added as a conclusion check.
candidates.instead: Needs CAND-7's job-counting mechanism first; then it is a one-line matrix row.

candidates.what: Each unit row stands for a whole pytest file, and the dashboard folds `pytest --collect-only` names into search. Collection is best-effort: a job that collects nothing says so.
candidates.would_catch: Nothing today -- but the failure mode is that a path moves upstream, collection silently returns zero, and the row reports 'no assurance' in a way a reader skims past. Worth asserting a minimum collected count per file so a move is loud.
candidates.instead: Assert collected > 0 per unit file, and fail the row if a previously-collecting file drops to zero.
